mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of valid passport of each director, shareholder, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport office or other competent government authority of the individual's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the country of issue; if the country is not a Hague Convention signatory, consular legalization through the Cayman Islands/UK consular post or embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement dated within three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or regulated financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a public notary followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Ownership Declaration and Source of Wealth Statement executed by the ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ultimate beneficial owner executing before a notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing, and Register of Members of any corporate shareholder or corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Cayman Islands General Registry or equivalent corporate registry of the jurisdiction of incorporation of the corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority; consular legalization if the originating registry is outside the Hague Apostille network

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and professional introduction from the existing transactional bank of the UBO or corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank letterhead with notarized signatory; apostille or consular legalization required where the bank cannot provide authenticated originals

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, officers, and authorized signatories against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, UK Consolidated List of Financial Sanctions Targets, EU Sanctions Map, and Cayman Islands Financial Reporting Authority notices. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs), family members, and close associates must receive enhanced due diligence, including independent source of funds and source of wealth verification, senior management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring for the entire business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Cayman Islands General Registry Corporate Portal (https://www.ciregistry.gov.ky)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be submitted in English or in a foreign script with a mandatory English translation and romanized transliteration. The proposed name must be distinguishable from existing entities, must not mislead as to the nature of business, and must not imply government connection, sovereign status, or regulated activities absent prior regulatory consent.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is valid for an initial 90-day period and may be extended for an additional 90 days by filing an extension request with the Cayman Islands General Registry before expiry. If the Registrar rejects a proposed name, the applicant may submit a formal written reconsideration request within 14 days of the rejection, providing distinguishability arguments and any letters of no objection from the relevant regulatory authority. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may apply to the Grand Court of the Cayman Islands for judicial review. Licensed corporate services providers may also liaise with the Registrar to clear sensitive tokens prior to incorporation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A physical registered office in the Cayman Islands is mandatory, and it may be located at the premises of a licensed registered office provider. A purely virtual or non-Cayman address is not permissible. If the Cayman Islands Economic Substance Law applies because the entity is tax resident in the Cayman Islands and carries on a relevant activity, additional physical presence in the Cayman Islands may be required.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 10% per annum for high-risk payment-service-sector licensees; the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority and the Financial Reporting Authority may conduct unannounced on-site inspections, particularly when AML/CFT and UBO record-keeping deficiencies are identified.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Cayman Islands Companies Act (2023 Revision), Part IV (Exempted Companies), sections 9, 26-28, 34 and 209; Tax Concessions Act (2021 Revision), section 6; UK Companies Act 2006, Part 34 (overseas company registration); UK Payment Services Regulations 2017 (SI 2017/752), Part 3 (authorisation of payment institutions)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cayman Islands Registrar of Companies, Companies Unit, General Registry, Grand Cayman; UK Companies House, Overseas Companies Team; UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), Authorisations Division
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation issued under section 21 of the Companies Act, following submission of Form 1 (Notice of Registration of an Exempted Company) and the Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital or escrow deposit is required for a Cayman Exempted Company; nominal capital of USD 1,000 suffices for incorporation. For FCA authorisation as a payment institution under PSR 2017, the applicant must hold initial capital of at least EUR 125,000 (EUR 50,000 if acquiring only), being paid-up share capital and reserves. Cayman law does not mandate escrow; safeguarding of customer payment funds is instead achieved by segregated trust accounts maintained at an authorised bank.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the incorporation of the Company as an exempted company under the Cayman Islands Companies Act is approved, and the subscribed shares be allotted and issued at par under the Articles. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the registered office be established at the office of the registered office provider in Grand Cayman, which provider shall maintain the statutory registers. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the persons named in the consent to act be appointed first directors, and that a President, Chief Financial Officer and Corporate Secretary be appointed as officers. RESOLVED THAT the Company register as an overseas company in the United Kingdom and apply to the Financial Conduct Authority for authorisation as a payment institution for its merchant acquiring and gateway business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cayman Islands General Registry, Companies Unit (acting through a licensed registered agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the licensed registered agent to submit a two-name priority reservation through the Registry e-filing portal with the draft Memorandum and Articles of Association. Complete beneficial ownership and sanctions screening of the proposed shareholder, directors and officers. Upon clearance, the Registry reserves the selected name for 90 days.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Shareholder and director due diligence file (KYC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for duplication or lack of distinctiveness, file the secondary reserved name or obtain a letter of non-objection from the prior holder, then resubmit the reservation within the 90-day window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation Filing and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of Companies, Cayman Islands General Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The registered agent files Form 1 (Notice of Registration of an Exempted Company) together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association and pays the CI$850 government fee. The Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation on the filing date; express same-day service is available for priority matters.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (exempted company)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar raises a query under section 11 regarding insufficient particulars, file a corrected Form 2 with precise objects and share capital provisions within 14 days and resubmit the complete exhibit set.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) — operating via the GOV.UK online portal; corporation tax and VAT registrations are handled through the Government Gateway and HMRC's 'Register for Corporation Tax' and 'Register for VAT' digital services. Customs declarations are made through the Customs Declaration Service (CDS). HMRC is headquartered at 100 Parliament Street, London SW1A 2BQ.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Cayman Exempted Company that is not incorporated in the UK but carries on a trade in the UK through a permanent establishment (PE), or makes taxable supplies of goods/services in the UK, must register for UK tax identifiers. Step 1 — Corporation Tax: register for a 10-digit Unique Taxpayer Reference (UTR) by submitting HMRC form CT41G (or the online 'Register an overseas company for Corporation Tax' service) within 3 months of starting to trade in the UK; a UK tax return (CT600) is required annually even where no UK tax is due. Step 2 — VAT: a non-established taxable person (NETP) must register for a GB VAT registration number from the first taxable supply in the UK (no £90,000 threshold applies to non-established businesses); registration is via HMRC form VAT1 (or the 'VATEC' non-established taxable person process, now delivered through HMRC online services); a UK tax representative may be required by HMRC (VATA 1994, Sch 1, para 10A) in cases of serious VAT non-compliance. Step 3 — Customs: obtain a GB EORI number via the HMRC online service for any import/export of goods. Step 4 — PAYE/employment taxes if the entity has UK employees. Step 5 — apply for the appropriate FCA authorisation (Authorised Payment Institution or Small Payment Institution under the Payment Services Regulations 2017) before handling funds; the FCA authorisation number is referenced in AML/tax filings. Where the entity operates a UK branch (PE), the overseas company branch must also be registered with Companies House under the Overseas Companies Regulations 2009 (Form OS BR1), and the registration number must be quoted alongside the UK UTR/VAT IDs.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The UK has no check-the-box election. A Cayman Exempted Company is treated as an opaque non-resident company under UK tax law and is chargeable to corporation tax only on profits attributable to a UK permanent establishment (CTA 2009, Part 4; TIOPA 2010 s 5). Available elections and filings: (i) the UK branch exemption election (CTA 2009 s 18A) is only available to UK-resident companies and therefore cannot be made by a Cayman entity for its UK PE; (ii) hybrid mismatch elections under TIOPA 2010 Part 6A (s 474) may be filed where double non-taxation arises from the Cayman entity's tax-exempt status in the Cayman Islands and a UK mismatch arrangement; (iii) for VAT, the entity may elect to use the VAT Mini One Stop Shop / One Stop Shop (MOSS/OSS) for B2C digital services, the annual accounting scheme, cash accounting scheme, or partial exemption special methods (e.g., bespoke capital goods method or standard partial exemption method under VATA 1994 s 26 and SI 1993/1741); (iv) an election under CTA 2009 s 196A to treat certain shares/derivatives for tax purposes; (v) where no UK PE exists but the company receives UK-source income subject to withholding tax, no UTR registration is mandatory but a claim to treaty relief may be made via HMRC's double taxation treaty claim form (UK-Cayman relations are governed only by a Tax Information Exchange Agreement and a Tax Cooperation Agreement, not a comprehensive double tax treaty, so most categories of UK-source income cannot be reduced below the statutory withholding rates).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value Added Tax) — UK national VAT administered by HMRC under the Value Added Tax Act 1994 and the VAT Regulations 1995 (SI 1995/251)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: £90,000 taxable turnover per rolling 12 months for UK-established businesses (from 1 April 2024); scheduled to rise to £100,000 on 1 April 2026. A non-established taxable person (NETP), including a Cayman Exempted Company, must register from the first taxable supply in the UK regardless of value. Separately, FCA-regulated payment institutions must also notify HMRC for Money Laundering Regulations supervision where they are not already supervised by FCA.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The UK does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping system for VAT invoices. However, 'Making Tax Digital for VAT' (MTD) is mandatory for all VAT-registered businesses (from April 2022), requiring: (i) digital record-keeping in MTD-compatible software; (ii) submission of VAT returns directly from those digital records via HMRC's MTD Application Programming Interfaces (APIs); (iii) tri-annual digital links between software packages; and (iv) penalties based on points for late or non-compliant submissions (Finance Act 2021 s 108, points-based late-submission/late-payment penalty regime effective from 1 January 2023). There is no requirement for pre-clearance of each invoice; however, e-invoices must comply with the UK VAT invoice content rules (VAT Regulations 1995, regs 13-16) and, for cross-border services, the place-of-supply and reverse-charge provisions of VATA 1994 ss 7A, 8 and Schedule 4A. Payment gateway services ('transactions concerning payments and transfers') are exempt financial services under VATA 1994 Sch 9 Group 5, so a PSP will generally be a partially exempt business subject to the input tax recovery rules, the annual partial exemption adjustment, and the capital goods scheme (VAT Regulations 1995 Part XIV).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: exports of goods from the UK are zero-rated at 0% under VATA 1994 s 30 and Schedule 8, Group 6 (supply of goods exported by the supplier) and Group 7 (supply of goods which it is intended to export), provided the goods are physically removed from the UK within the prescribed time limits (usually within 3 months of supply) and HMRC evidence requirements are met (VAT Regulations 1995, Part XVI, regs 116-131). Services for export: financial/payment processing services supplied to non-UK customers are normally outside the scope of UK VAT (B2B place of supply = customer's country under VATA 1994 s 7A and the place-of-supply rules) rather than zero-rated, or are VAT-exempt where they fall within Sch 9 Group 5; the 0% rate applies to services directly related to exported goods (e.g., freight, insurance) under Sch 8 Group 7A. A Cayman Exempted Company acting as a payment gateway will typically charge no UK VAT on B2B fees to overseas merchants because the customer belongs outside the UK, but it must retain robust digital evidence of the customer's business establishment (e.g., merchant's VAT ID, EC sales list references or treaty certificates) to support the outside-of-scope/zero-rated treatment in the UK VAT return.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CDS declaration, CHIEF legacy accepted for transitional cases), with the 32-digit Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Commercial invoice and packing list showing the overseas consignee and Incoterms 2020
Bill of Lading (sea) / Air Waybill (air) / CMR consignment note (road), evidencing physical departure of the goods from the UK
Evidence of the export value and method of payment (e.g., inward remittance certificate, SWIFT/MT103 advice or bank statement showing foreign currency receipt)
GB EORI number of the exporter
Proof of due diligence on the overseas counterparty (visa/mastercard settlement statements and merchant contracts for payment gateway fees)

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of England (BoE) acting as the central monetary authority; foreign exchange administration is effectively shared by HM Treasury, the Prudential Regulation Authority (PRA), and the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) for conduct, anti-money laundering, and sanctions compliance under the UK Money Laundering Regulations 2017 and OFSI sanctions framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The United Kingdom operates a fully liberalised capital and current account regime; the Exchange Control Act 1947 has been repealed in its entirety, leaving no statutory exchange controls, conversion quotas, or pre-approval requirements for cross-border fund transfers. Both current account transactions (trade, fees, royalties) and capital account transactions (equity injection, loans, dividends) may be freely converted into GBP and remitted overseas. The only operative discipline is compliance with sanctions, PEP screening, and anti-money laundering reporting; profit repatriation from a UK bank account held by a Cayman exempted company is not subject to any timing, amount, or conversion ratio restriction, provided the beneficial owner and transaction origin are transparent.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory obligation for UK-domiciled or UK-account-holding entities to surrender export receipts, repatriate foreign currency, or convert export proceeds into GBP within a prescribed timeline. A Cayman exempted company operating as a payment services provider through UK clearing rails is equally exempt from any mandatory surrender. However, as a regulated activity, all inbound and outbound settlement flows must maintain a complete audit trail, and cross-border transaction data must be reported to HMRC under the UK Payment Services Regulations 2017 and, when applicable, the BoE's International Transactions Reporting System for statistical purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low to Medium. UK-authorised electronic money institutions (e.g., Revolut Business, Tide, Currencycloud) generally require the customer to be a UK or EEA-incorporated trading entity with substantive local management; a pure Cayman exempted company without a UK branch and without FCA authorisation will typically be declined. Certain offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Leupay, Interpay) can onboard Cayman structures, but they are not direct members of UK Faster Payments or Bacs clearing systems and must route settlement through a UK sponsoring bank, which recreates the same KYC/AML burden. Therefore, a direct corporate banking relationship with a Tier 1 UK commercial bank remains the only viable long-term liquidity and clearing solution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is generally not permitted for an unlicensed Cayman exempted company whose business model is cross-border payment acquiring. Under the Joint Money Laundering Steering Group (JMLSG) guidance for high-risk third-country entities, a physical in-person interview of all directors, or at minimum the senior management team and the ultimate beneficial owner, is mandatory. The interview may be conducted at the bank's UK office or, in rare cases, via a notarised video appointment with a UK-recognised legal or compliance intermediary physically present. The bank will require original board resolutions, apostilled certificate of incorporation, a certified register of directors and shareholders, and a completed FBI/INTRA compliance questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cayman Islands jurisdiction flagged as a tax-haven by internal risk rating
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit Cayman Exempted Company Certificate of Incorporation, registered agent certificate, current standing from Cayman General Registry, tax residency certificate proving active management in the UK or confirming the Cayman entity's tax-exempt status under the Tax Exempted Company regime, plus an economic substance declaration showing that core income-generating activities are performed in the UK under the Cayman International Tax Co-operation (Economic Substance) Act amendment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk sector: Payment Service Provider with cross-border acquiring and settlement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a full compliance pack including FCA/OFAC sanctions screening policies, transaction monitoring and suspicious activity reporting procedures, PCI DSS v3.2.1 compliance evidence, audited financial statements for the last two years, any Cayman Islands regulatory license (if applicable under the Cayman Payment and Settlement Act), and a legally binding undertaking to establish a UK PSD2/AML senior management function and a physical UK registered office before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership complexity with nominee/director structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a complete shareholder register and director register, identity verification for every ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) including passport and proof of residential address, any trust deed or foundation constitutional documents, a signed declaration of beneficial ownership matching UK People with Significant Control (PSC) requirements, and audited source-of-funds evidence for each UBO showing legitimate accumulation path.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential sanctions exposure via offshore trading network
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present an independent third-party sanctions compliance audit issued by a global consulting firm within the last six months, evidence of real-time screening against the UK OFSI consolidated list, UN sanctions, and OFAC SDN list, a segmented geo-traffic analysis demonstrating zero transactions with sanctioned jurisdictions, and a procedural blocker-line protocol preventing accidental transshipment through sanctioned counterparties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections from the Cayman exempted company's shareholder or parent to the UK operating account must be routed via a correspondent banking network using a valid SWIFT/BIC and MT103 message with complete remitter details. Recommended UK Balance of Payments purpose codes: '7.1 - Investment by non-resident in UK subsidiaries' for equity injections, or '6.1 - Loans from direct investor' if structured as intercompany debt. The remitter must attach a board resolution approving the injection, a capital call notice or valuation statement, and source-of-funds documentation evidencing the lawful origin of the transfer. Correspondent banks will require the ordering bank to be a non-OFAC-sanctioned institution with a clean reputation; for non-USD/GBP currencies, the pair is first converted in the London FX market via a market maker before crediting the UK GBP account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Disbursements from the UK treasury account should be executed through a multi-rail clearing matrix: (a) vendor and service payments settle via SWIFT MT103 over the correspondent network, using purpose code '2.0 - Trade / Other services'; (b) merchant payouts in GBP below £1 million per day utilise UK Faster Payments (FPS) for near-instant settlement; (c) same-day high-value GBP transfers use CHAPS for irrevocable settlement; (d) acquiring receivables from Visa/Mastercard settle via association rails (VisaNet and Debit Card Settlement) through a UK Principal Member bank, with daily net settlement into the operational account; and (e) trade transactions requiring document scrutiny are supported by irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit issued by the UK bank under UCP600, using MT700/MT701 messages. Crypto-currency payouts are not recommended without a specific FCA activity authorisation and are excluded from the core clearing blueprint.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla FX forwards executed with an authorised UK bank or FCA-regulated EMI, subject to evidence of an underlying commercial transaction and no speculative intent
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) to hedge GBP exposure in restricted emerging-market currencies, with cash settlement in GBP and strict ISDA 2002 Master Agreement documentation
Cross-currency swaps for the interest rate and principal exchange between USD and GBP, executed under ISDA with a UK bank counterparty and reported to a UK EMIR Trade Repository

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Cayman Islands Annual Return and Annual Government Fee (Companies Act s.132; Exempted Company renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, Cayman Islands General Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 January of each calendar year on a fixed calendar-year cycle; no anniversary deferral for an operating exempted company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic statutory late penalty at 10% of the annual fee accrues from 1 February; penalties escalate for continued default; persistent non-payment triggers administrative strike-off/discontinuation, loss of certificate of good standing, and a Grand Court restoration process at significant additional cost.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No corporate income tax for Cayman exempted companies on foreign-sourced income; local operations may attract tax but payment gateway activities are structured to qualify for full exemption

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cayman Islands Tax Return Form (Form 1), filed electronically via Tax Information Authority portal at tia.gov.ky
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after the end of the accounting period

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or loss after all adjustments and deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report solely Cayman-sourced income; foreign income is exempt and excluded
Include only Cayman-sourced receipts; foreign revenue excluded

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: CI$500 late-filing penalty plus CI$50 per day (capped at CI$5,000); non-filing constitutes criminal offence with potential license revocation

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Cayman Islands maintains no bilateral tax treaties with the United Kingdom; no withholding tax applies and TRC submission is unnecessary
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% for royalties and interest as no withholding tax regime exists

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Cayman$100,000 (approx. US$120,000) for mandatory local-file documentation where local activities exceed threshold
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Cayman Economic Substance Regulations apply; cross-border payment gateway services may qualify as a relevant activity requiring adequate employees, premises and core income-generating activities in Cayman

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating income, omitting Cayman-sourced revenue or failing to file the tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to CI$10,000, imprisonment up to two years and potential deregistration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable; possible disqualification, fines and criminal prosecution for willful evasion

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to perform customer due diligence or report suspicious transactions in payment services
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to CI$100,000 and license revocation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines, imprisonment and prohibition from directorships

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating without adequate economic substance for relevant payment processing activities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to CI$100,000 and potential criminal penalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for penalties and possible imprisonment for deliberate non-compliance
